The context only partly answers this. It shows how the nav spec `v^v` is parsed, but not what the search covers in the end.

- `NavPlan.parse` reads `v` as down and `^` as up (src/nav.zig:44-45). It sets `has_ceiling` for a down-then-up pair and `has_trampoline` for an up-then-down pair (src/nav.zig:62-65).
- `v^v` is down, up, down. That gives `has_ceiling` at the first pair (`v^`) and `has_trampoline` at the second (`^v`). So both flags are set, going by the parse loop (src/nav.zig:59-66).
- With `has_trampoline` set, `shouldScanFiles` returns false at depth 0, so files in the root directory are skipped. Deeper files are scanned (src/nav.zig:77-82).
- `shouldRecurseSubdirs` is not shown (it is at src/nav.zig:85-90). I therefore can't say how `has_ceiling` interacts with the trampoline, or whether subdirectories are searched at all.
- The tests cover only `v^` and `^v` separately (src/nav.zig:109-123). None covers `v^v`.

Missing: the body of `shouldRecurseSubdirs`, and any README/GUIA text on `--nav`.
